rows.title: Database Schema Definition API now supports creation of generated columns

body: The attribute Drupal\Core\Update\Attribute\MarkFutureUpdateEquivalent has been added to make it possible to register hook_update_N implementations as equivalent during module install. Previously, registering updates as equivalent was only possible during module updates, because hook_update_N implementations do not run on module install. Applying the MarkFutureUpdateEquivalent attribute to the hook_update_N function will the register equivalent updates during both module install and update. The hook_update_N itself can be a no-op. If your site uses Drupal\Core\Update\UpdateHookRegistry::markFut
rows.title: MarkFutureUpdateEquivalent attribute added to register equivalent updates on site install

body: Display and form view mode configuration dependencies are recalculated to ensure all dependencies are recorded. View modes implement widget plugins which may have module dependencies. Previously, if a view mode implemented the same widget multiple times with different dependencies, then only one of those dependencies would be saved in the configuration's dependency list. This could cause situations where a module could be uninstalled without warning that a configuration depended on it. Site owners must ensure that updates are executed after upgrading to get the recalculated dependencies.
rows.title: View mode dependencies are recalculated

body: PostgreSQL merge queries now execute as a single native MERGE statement On PostgreSQL, $connection->merge($table)->...->execute() now runs one native MERGE statement. Before this change, the driver used the generic emulation: a SELECT followed by an INSERT or an UPDATE. The native statement uses RETURNING merge_action() to report the action taken. Return values are unchanged: Merge::STATUS_INSERT , Merge::STATUS_UPDATE , or NULL when the row existed and no update was requested. Modules need no code changes. The generic emulation is still used when: the condition targets a table other than the
rows.title: PostgreSQL merge query executes as a single native merge query

body: PostgreSQL has no LIKE or regular expression operators for non-text types such as integers. The pgsql driver rewrote all SQL in Connection::prepareStatement() to add a ::text type-cast to fields used with these operators. Relying on this rewrite for SQL passed as a string is deprecated in Drupal 11.5.0. The rewrite is removed in Drupal 13.0.0. Query builder queries are not affected. Their conditions get the type-cast when they are compiled. Before (deprecated): $result = $connection->query('SELECT [name] FROM {test} WHERE [age] LIKE :pattern', [':pattern' => '2%']); After, either add the cast
rows.title: PostgreSQL type-casting of fields in raw SQL with LIKE and regex operators is deprecated

body: A new static method, \Drupal\Core\Recipe\RecipeRunner::isApplying() has been added so that code can determine if it is being run when a recipe is being applied. For example: use \Drupal\Core\Recipe\RecipeRunner; function hook_install($is_syncing): void { // Set general module variables. $variable = RecipeRunner::isApplying() ? 'barbar', 'bar'; \Drupal::state()->set('my_module.foo', $variable); }

body: Node reference fields have a new setting, "Include unpublished nodes the user has access to view". It is off by default, so nothing changes for existing fields. Before, these fields only matched published nodes unless the user had the "Bypass content access control" permission. A user who was allowed to view unpublished nodes still could not reference them. When the setting is on, the nodes a user can reference follow the permissions they already have: "View any unpublished content": any unpublished node. "View own unpublished content": their own unpublished nodes. Neither: published nodes onl
rows.title: Node reference fields can include unpublished nodes the user may view

body: \Drupal\file\Element\ManagedFile::valueCallback() now validates #file_value_callbacks entries the same way core validates #process , #pre_render , and other render callbacks. Previously, #file_value_callbacks executed any callable directly, bypassing the protections added by #2966327: Limit what can be called by a callback in render arrays to reduce the risk of RCE . This allowed arbitrary code execution if untrusted input reached this property. Each callback must now be one of: A method tagged with the \Drupal\Core\Security\Attribute\TrustedCallback attribute. A method of a class implementing

body: drupalSettings.path.currentQuery , set by system_js_settings_alter() , is deprecated in drupal:12.0.0 and is removed from drupal:13.0.0. It has no cache context, so query string values could leak into cached pages. Custom or contributed JavaScript that reads drupalSettings.path.currentQuery must read the current query from window.location instead. Before: const query = drupalSettings.path.currentQuery; After: const query = new URLSearchParams(window.location.search);
rows.summary: removal introduced in an unstated version
rows.title: drupalSettings.path.currentQuery is deprecated

body: New strnatcasecmp and natcasesort functions in Drupal\Core\Utility\NaturalSort to introduce a generic sort helper for language-dependent string comparisons using a "natural order" algorithm as drop-in replacement for php functions strnatcasecmp and natcasesort . If php intl extension is installed it uses Collator::compare() , fallback to strnatcasecmp() Replace: strnatcasecmp($a_string, $b_string); With: NaturalSort::strnatcasecmp($a_string, $b_string); Replace: natcasesort($array); With: NaturalSort::natcasesort($array);

rows.summary: Drupal secure-code documentation says data must never be concatenated directly into SQL queries and directs developers to use proper argument substitution, select queries, escapeLike() for LIKE values, and fixed operator choices.

rows.title: Twig output escaping should not be bypassed without trusted data

rows.summary: SOURCE FACT: the Drupal update-status release-history feed can attach a Release type taxonomy term whose literal value is "Insecure" to an individual Drupal core release row. PROJECT JOIN: a future finding evaluator may match this only when the Project Analyzer observed installed Drupal core version matches that exact release row in the canonical reviewed release lifecycle context. DRUPAL SEMANTICS (reviewed): For Drupal Update Manager release metadata, a release carrying Release type "Insecure" is treated as insecure; when that exact release is installed, Drupal assigns NOT_SECURE status, whose documented meaning is that the project is missing security update(s). LIMITS: this reviewed meaning does not establish an exploit path, a specific CVE identifier, a finding severity level, or any compromise claim about a project.
rows.title: Drupal release metadata can attach the literal "Insecure" Release type term to a core release row

rows.summary: The official Drupal update-status release-history feed exposes project status, supported branches, release versions, release types, and security coverage, so release-aware knowledge should watch that source instead of hard-coding the latest Drupal version.
rows.title: Drupal core release state comes from the official update feed
